images.title: One factor for both terms
images.purpose: Shows 14 : 21 becoming 6 : 9 when both terms are multiplied by the same fractional factor 3/7.
images.composition: Two ratios stacked vertically in the centre, joined by two parallel down arrows sharing one label. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Top: the ratio '14 : 21' in large teal (#0072B2) digits. Bottom: the ratio '6 : 9' in large amber (#E69F00) digits, directly below. Two reddish purple (#CC79A7) arrows point straight down, one from 14 to 6 and one from 21 to 9; between them a single label '× 3/7 for both'. To the right, in small dark outline colour (#2B2B2B) text, the line '6 ÷ 14 = 3/7'. Exactly 2 ratios, 2 arrows.

images.takeaway: Find the factor from the known pair, then multiply the other term by the same factor.
images.description: Shows 14 : 21 becoming 6 : 9 when both terms are multiplied by the same fractional factor 3/7.
images.teaching_notes: The other two blanks (28 : 42 and 2 : 3) stay in the video and practice.

image_decisions.why: The fractional factor is the surprising case of this concept, and one clean diagram of the shared factor makes it visible.
